heading: Kotlin suspends for a real Yon endpoint
summary: A Kotlin HTTPClient is an interface whose methods are `suspend fun` without a body, such as `suspend fun read(): Greeting`. Tachyon writes the method and reads the answer into the `Greeting` data class from `client/models`; an answer of another shape gives a `Behaviors.Failure` whose code is `HTTP_RESPONSE`, and a failed request gives the code of the browser transport, such as `HTTP_STATUS`. A service gets the client with `@Needs private val greetingClient: GreetingClient` and calls it from a `suspend fun`. While the method waits for the server, the page keeps working, and the page gets a promise that settles when the method returns. `GreetingSetup` adds no adapter, so the request goes to the server of the page: the same origin, without cookies. `Cached` lets the browser cache answer a read, and after a successful `ClearCache` the next read asks the server again. `OverrideSetup` gives `OverrideClient` its own adapter, and that adapter answers instead of the network. Removing the component cancels the request, and the promise is rejected with the code `CANCELLED`. The server half of this example is a plain JavaScript controller. A controller in TypeScript, Python, PHP, Java, Groovy, C#, F#, Kotlin, Rust, Go, Dart, Ruby, Lua or C++ answers in the same way (see Controllers), so this section shows only the browser side in other languages.
